faqs.q: Do you manufacture the roofing yourselves?
faqs.a: Yes. We manufacture long-run roofing, cladding, spouting and flashings in our own Christchurch factory, which is how we keep turnaround times fast and quality consistent.

faqs.q: Can I buy supply-only, or do you install as well?
faqs.a: Both. We manufacture and supply product for your own builder, and we have our own installation team for complete supply and install jobs.

faqs.q: Can you price from my house plans?
faqs.a: Yes, use the Price Your Plans service. Send your plans through the contact form and we measure and price your roofing, cladding and spouting from the drawings.

faqs.q: What is the difference between corrugate and Roofdeck?
faqs.a: Corrugate is the classic round-profile iron, through-fixed with screws, and works from about 8 degrees pitch. Roofdeck is a trapezoidal long-run profile with stronger spanning and a flatter look, working from lower pitches. Both come in ColorCote finishes.

faqs.q: My roof is 4 degrees. Which Roofline profiles can I use?
faqs.a: Roofdeck and Everest Tray are the two Roofline profile options to consider at 4 degrees: both are treated as suitable from about 3 degrees when correctly designed and installed. Corrugate is treated as requiring about 8 degrees. Below 3 degrees, a membrane or low-slope roof system is the option to consider rather than these sheet profiles. Have the Roofline team confirm the final specification for the site.

faqs.q: The house is about 150 metres from the sea. Does that change the product or coating?
faqs.a: Yes. A site around 150 metres from the sea should be treated as demanding coastal exposure. MagnaFlow is the starting coating to consider, and AlumiGard may be more appropriate where the site is classed as very severe marine or is highly salt-exposed. Gauge and coating do different jobs: gauge is the material thickness, while the coating addresses corrosion exposure. Confirm the final coating and warranty specification for the exact site with the Roofline team.
The ColorCote and Zincalume colour ranges cover the popular New Zealand roof colours. Visit the colour options page or ask us for a specific colour match.

Roofline lists asbestos removal within its roofing solutions. Because asbestos work needs the right site controls and process, the team should confirm the approach for your particular roof before work is planned.

faqs.q: How long does a re-roof take?
faqs.a: Roofline says a residential re-roof can typically be completed in a few working days, weather permitting. The actual programme depends on roof size, detailing, access, product preparation and site conditions.

Roofline is Christchurch and Canterbury based. For a project outside the immediate Christchurch area, confirm the site location with the team so they can advise whether they can supply, install or both.
